# Literature search ledger

Search date: 21 July 2026. Search objective: locate the closest prior theorem on conditional heat-kernel concentration under a locally frustrated central staple pattern, and verify the formal hypotheses behind the claimed Dobrushin/product-domination consequence.

## Databases and query families

Publicly indexed records and primary publisher/article pages were screened through INSPIRE, arXiv, zbMATH Open, MathNet, SIAM, Wiley, Springer, APS, Elsevier/ScienceDirect metadata, OSTI, and institutional article repositories. Web-indexed MathSciNet queries were attempted; a subscription result interface was not available in this environment. No priority claim relies on an assertion of exhaustive database coverage.

| Query family | Representative exact queries | Screened outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Conditional theorem language | `"p_t(U)" "p_t(-U)" lattice gauge`; `"conditional" "heat-kernel action" lattice gauge`; `frustrated boundary conditions conditional probability lattice gauge theory center staple` | No matching theorem found. Results were unrelated, recent unrefereed mass-gap claims, or general lattice-gauge pages. |
| Dobrushin and gauge fields | `Dobrushin uniqueness condition lattice gauge theory compact Lie group weak coupling`; `site:inspirehep.net "Dobrushin" "lattice gauge"`; `site:mathscinet.ams.org "lattice gauge" Dobrushin` | Located the original Dobrushin paper and general criterion literature, but no paper testing the coefficient with the present central one-link construction. |
| Heat-kernel action | `"heat kernel action" lattice gauge theory Menotti Onofri`; `uniform Varadhan heat kernel compact Riemannian manifold small time` | Included Menotti–Onofri for the action and Varadhan's two 1967 papers for the logarithmic heat-kernel input. |
| Center and twisted boundaries | `center flux twisted boundary conditions lattice gauge theory primary paper 't Hooft`; `twisted partition functions lattice gauge theories center flux theorem`; citation-chain queries for Mack–Petkova and de Forcrand–von Smekal | Included primary sources on global twists, vortex free energies, and flux sectors. They retain global free-energy costs and do not state the local conditional theorem. |
| Constructive RG | `Balaban renormalization group approach lattice gauge field theories small fields large fields DOI`; citation-chain searches for Parts I–II and large fields | Included Balaban's small-field, cluster-expansion, and large-field papers. Their object and mechanism differ from a boundary-uniform one-link estimate. |
| Product domination | `Liggett Schonmann Stacey domination by product measures DOI 1997`; conditional-probability domination queries | Included the original product-domination paper to identify the relevant worst-conditioning hypothesis. |
| Low dimensions and center-free cases | `local center frustration lattice gauge theory boundary condition plaquette`; group-specific searches | No source located that removes the nontrivial-center hypothesis for this exact argument. The manuscript makes no such extension. |

## Included primary sources

1. Menotti and Onofri, heat-kernel lattice action, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(81)90560-5).
2. Varadhan, fundamental-solution asymptotics, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1002/cpa.3160200210), and diffusion small-time asymptotics, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1002/cpa.3160200404).
3. Dobrushin, conditional-probability regularity criterion, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1137/1113026).
4. Liggett–Schonmann–Stacey, product domination, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1214/aop/1024404279).
5. 't Hooft, electric/magnetic flux and twisted boundaries, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(79)90595-9).
6. Mack–Petkova, vortex-condensation sufficient condition, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(80)90121-9).
7. de Forcrand–von Smekal, SU(2) flux-sector free energies, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.66.011504).
8. Balaban, small-field effective actions, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01215223); cluster expansions, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01239022); large-field completion, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01238433).

## Excluded or contextual records

- Recent 2026 repository manuscripts claiming Yang–Mills mass-gap results were excluded from theorem grounding: they are not the closest source for the finite conditional calculation, and repository presence is not validation.
- General reviews and encyclopedia pages were used only to discover citation chains, not as support for theorem or priority claims.
- Global twisted-boundary simulations were excluded from the closest-theorem slot because they compare flux-sector partition functions rather than a local regular conditional kernel.
- Scalar or Abelian constructive models were excluded from the direct comparison because the paper's theorem is a finite non-Abelian compact-group conditional obstruction.

## Priority status

The search did not locate the same combination of: private-link realization of one central incident staple; compact-group metric barycenter LDP; exact target-good exponent; open positive-measure stability; and `m`-coefficient Dobrushin row obstruction. This is evidence for a contribution boundary, not a proof of priority. The manuscript therefore avoids “first,” “unprecedented,” and “no prior work.” A fresh MathSciNet/zbMATH/INSPIRE/arXiv search is required immediately before external submission.
